chunks: Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the policy of the Imam regarding the land that was conquered after the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.
He said: “Indeed, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام conducted himself among the people of Iraq with a policy that is an exemplar for all other lands.”

And he said: “The jizyah is not removed from the land of jizyah. Rather, the jizyah is the allotment of the mujāhidīn, while the charities belong to their people whom Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, named in His Book; they have no share of the jizyah.”

Then he عليه السلام said: “How vast justice is! Indeed, people become free of need when justice is established among them, and the sky sends down its provision and the earth brings forth its blessing by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

key_terms.الصَّدَقَاتُ: charitable funds allocated to their designated recipients
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the divinely guided leader with authority over communal affairs
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةِ: the poll-tax due from designated non-Muslim subjects in this legal context
key_terms.الْعَدْلَ: justice in governance and social order
key_terms.الْمُجَاهِدِينَ: those engaged in jihad, who are assigned this fiscal allotment here
key_terms.رِزْقَهَا: the provision sent down from the sky
key_terms.سِيرَةِ: governing policy or mode of conduct

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about jizyah, public revenue, and justice under the Imam’s governance?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the policy of the Imam concerning lands conquered after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, presenting the conduct of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام in Iraq as the governing model. It distinguishes between jizyah and charities in fiscal distribution, and concludes by emphasizing that justice brings communal sufficiency and divine blessing.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1677 - Muhammad ibn Muslim asked Abu Ja’far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) about the policy of the Imam concerning the lands conquered after the Prophet of Allah (swt), peace and blessings be upon him and his family.
The Imam (as) replied: "Indeed, Amir al-Mu'minin (Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as)) established a policy in Iraq that serves as a model for all other lands."

He added: "The jizya is never lifted from the lands of jizya. It is the due of the fighters (mujahideen), while sadaqat is designated for those whom Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious, has specified in His Book. They (the fighters) have no share in the jizya."

The Imam then said: "How expansive justice is! When people are treated justly, they will prosper. The skies will send down their sustenance, and the earth will yield its blessings by the permission of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious."
